event.title: Dancin’ in the Streets: A Simchat Torah Celebration
event.description:
6:00 pm: Class with Rabbi Jenna
6:30 pm: Happy Hour
7:30 pm: Service and dancing

Simchat Torah, which means “Rejoicing in Torah,” is the day when we gather to renew ourselves as we begin the cycle of reading from Genesis once again. Let loose and dance like no one’s watching as you enjoy live music, themed cocktails and mocktails, and lively dancing on I Street.

Before the main event, choose from taking a class with Rabbi Jenna diving into the holiday and exploring the first few lines of the Torah, or get social and meet new people at our happy hour.

Class: Make it Make Sense

On Simchat Torah, we read the very first lines of Torah and the story of creation – not making something out of nothing but rather creating order out of chaos – tohu va-vohu. In a world that at times feels too chaotic to comprehend, how can we continue to create meaningful and joyful experiences? Explore these big questions and more through a text study with Rabbi Jenna.

Must be 21+ and present ID to attend. No one will be turned away from any of our programs due to lack of funds. For more information, please contact our Director of Jewish Life,  Nathan.

event.title: Small Groups, Big Questions
event.description:
These five-week meetups offer a space to think through life’s big questions using a Jewish framework. Led by Sixth & I’ers in Eckington, Pentagon City, and in Chinatown (at Sixth & I), these salon-style gatherings are a great way to meet new people in a relaxed, laid-back setting.   

You’ll discuss:

  • Week 1: Intro
  • Week 2: Individuality vs. Communal Belonging 
  • Week 3: How do you make big decisions?  
  • Week 4: What makes a meaningful friendship? 
  • Week 5: How to say goodbye 

Apply for a fall 2026 cohort by September 30. 

Get to Know the Facilitators: 

Travis (he/him)
Thursdays, October 8 – November 5 from 7:00 pm – 8:30 pm at Sixth & I
Travis grew up in Maryland and has lived in Rockville since 2016. He is an active musician who directs an LGBTQ+ community jazz band in DC. Travis is excited to help foster Jewish community and meet new people.

Taylor (she/her)
Mondays, November 2 – 30 from 7:00 pm – 8:30 pm in Eckington
Taylor is a GA/NC southerner turned “what do you do for work” Washingtonian. She finished the Jewish Welcome Workshop and officially converted in July 2026. She works as a documentary filmmaker and lives on a non-profit farm in the heart of DC (which is definitely not a commune).

No one will be turned away from any of our programs due to lack of funds. For more information, please contact our Director of Community Engagement, Christy.

event.title: CHELSEA WOLFE: THE DARK – WORLD TOUR
event.description:
Listen to Chelsea Wolfe

Acclaimed musician, songwriter, and multidisciplinary artist Chelsea Wolfe returns with new music at the center of a world that she is only beginning to reveal. “The Dark” and “Death is Not the End” arrive after a week of fan speculation, sparked by cryptic imagery, fragments of sound, and the shadowy visual language teased by Heretic Parfum across its socials.

Wolfe has become one of the most singular artists in the world, moving fluidly between doom metal, folk, industrial, electronic music, and spectral balladry. She has collaborated with artists including Deftones’ Chino Moreno, Xiu Xiu, and Converge, had her music featured in HBO’s “Game of Thrones,” co-wrote the score for the A24 horror film X with Tyler Bates, and turned heads at last year’s Ann Demeulemeester show at Paris Fashion Week.

Known for building immersive worlds where darkness and beauty are indistinguishable, Wolfe has cultivated a devoted global following through music that explores transformation, spirituality, grief, longing, and the unseen forces that shape our lives. With these new songs and GHOSTS arriving in close succession, she opens the door to a new chapter that feels unmistakably her own.

event.title: JOSH THOMAS: JIGGLE, JIGGLE
event.description:
Josh Thomas burst onto the Australian comedy scene when he became the youngest ever winner of Raw Comedy, the prestigious national competition produced by the Melbourne Comedy Festival. Two years later, while still in his teens, he received a Melbourne Comedy Festival nomination for Best Show.

Thomas is best known for writing, acting, and co-executive producing his own TV show, “Please Like Me,” inspired by his life, which was named one of the best TV shows of the year by Entertainment Weekly, The New Yorker, and Time. His writing for the show won awards from the Australian Academy (AACTA) and the Australian Writers Guild. The show won Best Comedy at the AACTA Awards, Most Outstanding Comedy at the Logie Awards, and was nominated as Best Comedy at the International Emmy Awards, Rose d’Or Awards, and GLAAD Media Awards. Thomas also created and starred in the TV show, “Everything’s Gonna Be Okay.” He recently launched a weekly podcast, “Josh Thomas and Friends and You,” featuring conversations with his friends.

event.title: Simone Dinnerstein, piano
event.description:
Listen to Simone Dinnerstein

Lauded by The Washington Post as “an artist of strikingly original ideas and irrefutable integrity,” Simone Dinnerstein returns for an evening of distinctive artistry. The program opens with Rameau’s rarely performed Gavotte et six doubles, followed by American composer Philip Lasser’s Twelve Variations on Chorale by J.S. Bach, exploring the power and modernity of Bach’s harmonic poetry. Dinnerstein continues to demonstrate her “unique voice in the forest of Bach interpretation” (The New York Times) with the composer’s 15 Sinfonias, and closes her program with Keith Jarrett’s Encore from “Tokyo,” ending the night on a note of otherworldly serenity. 

Dinnerstein’s performance is the fifth-annual Ruth Bader Ginsburg Memorial Recital—a creative initiative connecting Justice Ginsburg’s love of music, the esteemed artists she championed and befriended, and the future of the vocal and instrumental arts in which she delighted. 

Program:
Rameau – Gavotte et six doubles
Lasser – Twelve Variations on Chorale by J.S. Bach
Bach – 15 Sinfonias, BWV 787-801
Jarrett / trans. Uwe Karcher – Encore from “Tokyo” 

Photo by Lisa-Marie Mazzucco

event.title: How to be a Jewish Adult
event.description:
This 8-week workshop meets Tuesdays starting October 20, with some exceptions. The full dates are Tuesdays, October 20, 27, November 3, 10, 17, December 1, 8, and 15 from 6:30 – 8:30 pm.

Do you ever feel like you could use a handbook for how to build a Jewish life? If you identify as Jewish or Jew-ish but aren’t sure how to incorporate Judaism into your day-to-day life, this 8-week series offers equal parts community-building and deep-dive into core lessons from our tradition to help you feel more Jewishly connected. 

Led by Rabbi Loren Berman, each class will take on an essential Jewish value or teaching including big topics ranging from love and relationships, social justice, unpacking what it means to be spiritual, and more. In a judgement-free space, you’ll consider how to apply these teachings to your life in a way that feels personal, meaningful, and authentic to you as you build community with others in their 20s and 30s who are curious to engage with Judaism in practical and profound ways.

About Rabbi Loren Berman
Guest Rabbi Loren Berman has taught and mentored at Sixth & I since moving to DC in 2023. Currently a full-time consultant in the public sector, he previously worked with Jews in their 20s and 30s at Sefaria and Moishe House.

No one will be turned away from any of our classes due to lack of funds. For more information, please contact our Jewish Life Associate, Robyn.

event.title: Jewish Page Turners: A Book Club
event.description:
At our monthly book club, read a book recommended by our rabbis, share your takeaways, and reflect on how the book relates to your own experience of Judaism and spirituality.

October’s book is The Amen Effect: Ancient Wisdom to Mend Our Broken Hearts and World by Rabbi Sharon Brous. In our current era of loneliness and isolation, discuss how we can better come together, deepen connections, and build community.

  • Bad Jews: A History of American Jewish Politics and Identities by Emily Tamkin

event.title: Niladri Kumaar, sitar
event.description:
Listen to Niladri Kumaar

Niladri Kumaar, sitar
Agnelo Fernandes, keys
Sambit Chatterjee, drums
Satyajit Talwalkar, tabla 

Celebrated sitar maestro Niladri Kumaar is a compelling force in Indian classical music and an innovator who carries centuries of tradition in every note. This evening is both a forward-looking showcase and a tribute to an irreplaceable musical bond: curated selections from Space Between the Notes, the only recorded live performance between Kumaar and the late, legendary Zakir Hussain. Their singular partnership resounds once more—a gift, before the album’s release later this year.

Featuring sitar, zitar, and an ensemble of Indian and American musicians with jazz influences, this is Indian music at its most expansive, where centuries of classical tradition meet improvisational spirit. 

Program:
“The Space Between the Notes”

Photo courtesy of Nilandri Kumaar Archives

event.title: Minsoo Sohn, piano
event.description:
Listen to Minsoo Sohn

“A genuine artist, with a thoughtfully conceived and poetic interpretation.” – The New York Times

Pianist Minsoo Sohn debuts with Washington Performing Arts for a program exhibiting his undeniable musical intelligence and masterful virtuosity. Studied by the likes of Beethoven and Mozart, Bach’s The Well-Tempered Clavier, Book I, is frequently regarded as one of the most significant works in the history of classical music. Sohn brings his own poetic interpretation to this storied collection of 24 prelude and fugue pairs, creating an unforgettable evening with one of the most audacious and influential works for piano as the centerpiece.

Known for his career as a devoted pedagogue, Sohn is also recognized as the teacher of Yunchan Lim, the youngest first-prize winner in the history of the Van Cliburn International Piano Competition. 

Program:
J.S. Bach – The Well-Tempered Clavier, Book I

event.title: How to be a Jewish Adult
event.description:
This 8-week workshop meets Tuesdays starting October 20, with some exceptions. The full dates are Tuesdays, October 20, 27, November 3, 10, 17, December 1, 8, and 15 from 6:30 – 8:30 pm.

Do you ever feel like you could use a handbook for how to build a Jewish life? If you identify as Jewish or Jew-ish but aren’t sure how to incorporate Judaism into your day-to-day life, this 8-week series offers equal parts community-building and deep-dive into core lessons from our tradition to help you feel more Jewishly connected. 

Led by Rabbi Loren Berman, each class will take on an essential Jewish value or teaching including big topics ranging from love and relationships, social justice, unpacking what it means to be spiritual, and more. In a judgement-free space, you’ll consider how to apply these teachings to your life in a way that feels personal, meaningful, and authentic to you as you build community with others in their 20s and 30s who are curious to engage with Judaism in practical and profound ways.

Guest Rabbi Loren Berman has taught and mentored at Sixth & I since moving to DC in 2023. Currently a full-time consultant in the public sector, he previously worked with Jews in their 20s and 30s at Sefaria and Moishe House.

No one will be turned away from any of our classes due to lack of funds. For more information, please contact our Jewish Life Associate, Robyn.

event.title: Aga Khan Master Musicians
event.description:
Listen to the Aga Khan Master Musicians

Aga Khan Master Musicians
Basel Rajoub, saxophone and clarinet
Feras Charestan, qanun
Yurdal Tokcan, oud
Abbos Kosimov, drum
Vincent Peirani, accordion

Washington Performing Arts presents an evening where the musical worlds of Central Asia, China, the Middle East, and contemporary Europe meet in striking and unexpected harmony. Five performers from the Aga Khan Master Musicians—an artistic collective dedicated to living musical traditions—are joined by celebrated French artist Vincent Peirani for a concert that is wholly its own.

Syrian-born Basel Rajoub has reimagined an entirely new vocabulary for the saxophone; his compatriot Feras Charestan commands the qanun, the shimmering Middle Eastern plucked zither. Turkish oud master Yurdal Tokcan and Uzbek percussionist Abbos Kosimov, a virtuoso on the doira frame drum, complete the collective’s lineup. They are joined by Vincent Peirani, award-winning accordionist, singer, and composer whose work spans jazz, contemporary music, and improvisation. Six distinct voices in one extraordinary evening.

Photos courtesy of AKMP, Sebastian Schutyser, and Stan Augris

event.title: Haley Heynderickx
event.description:
Listen to Haley Heynderickx

Following the release of her acclaimed debut I Need to Start a Garden and its long-awaited follow-up Seed of a Seed, Haley Heynderickx recently released What of Our Nature, a collaboration with Max García Conover. After a year of touring with Garcia and working on new material, she now returns to the road for a rare run of solo performances.

One of contemporary folk’s most quietly captivating voices, Heynderickx writes with warmth, wit, and self-reflection. Her songs find wonder in the everyday while exploring questions of identity, belonging, and our relationship with the natural world. Tender, thoughtful and quietly spellbinding, these shows are an invitation to step into the unknown with her and leave a little room for what may come next.

event.title: Seth Parker Woods, cello, and Conor Hanick, piano
event.description:
Listen to Seth Parker Woods
Listen to Conor Hanick

Cellist Seth Parker Woods and pianist Conor Hanick unite for an evening of commanding musicianship at the intersection of tradition and discovery. A three-time GRAMMY nominee, Woods has garnered a reputation for versatile and inventive musicality, and is joined by pianist Hanick, praised for his precision with classic and contemporary fare.

Their program brings together Fazil Say’s vivid Four Cities, George Walker’s 1956 Sonata for cello and piano—of which Gramophone writes that Woods and Hanick’s recording is “more compellingly characterful,” with “the raw vulnerability of the central slow movement” lingering in the memory — and Rachmaninoff’s sweeping Cello Sonata, op. 19, one of the most passionate works in the duo repertoire.

Program:
Fazil Say – Four Cities
George Walker – Sonata for cello and piano (1956)
Sergei Rachmaninoff – Cello Sonata, op. 19 

Photos courtesy of Ben Gibbs and Rob Davidson

event.title: Balourdet Quartet
event.description:
Listen to the Balourdet Quartet

Recipient of the 2024 Avery Fisher Career Grant and Chamber Music America’s Cleveland Quartet Award, the Balourdet Quartet was born from late-night chamber music sessions and became one of the most celebrated young ensembles in the world. Described as “unafraid to show its personality,” their playing balances clarity with expressive warmth, and a deep belief that music exists to break down walls. Their Washington Performing Arts program reflects that ambition: spanning four centuries from Monteverdi to Ben Johnston’s microtonal meditation on “Amazing Grace,” with Bartók’s haunted and personal Sixth Quartet, and Mendelssohn’s passionately constructed Second at the center. 

Program:
Claudio Monteverdi (arr. Benjamin Zannoni) – Selection of Madrigals
Béla Bartók – String Quartet No. 6, Sz. 85
Ben Johnston – String Quartet No. 4, “Amazing Grace”
Felix Mendelssohn – String Quartet No. 2 in A Minor, op. 13 

Photo by Luke Ratray

event.title: Anthony “Tony” Walker & Friends
event.description:
Listen to Anthony “Tony” Walker

Washington, DC, has given the music world some of the most transcendent voices in American music. Longtime Washington Performing Arts Children of the Gospel Choir music director and accompanist, producer, educator, and DMV-area luminary Anthony “Tony” Walker leads an evening celebrating the legendary Roberta Flack, Marvin Gaye, Donnie Hathaway, and Richard Smallwood, whose roots in DC’s Black communities helped shape the sound of a nation. Part concert, part storytelling, the evening weaves the music and the stories together to celebrate the people and places behind the songs you know by heart.

Photo by Ashera J Photography

event.title: Paul Huang, violin
event.description:
Listen to Paul Huang

Four acclaimed musicians join together in a powerful program meditating on time, loss, and hope. Bela Kovacs’ Sholem Alekhem, rov Feidman! is a vibrant clarinet homage to klezmer song and spirit, laughter edged with lament. It casts light on the echoes that follow, reminding us that even in the face of ruin, sound endures. Shostakovich’s Piano Trio No. 2, written amid war and loss, spins a ghostly klezmer dance: ironic, grief-stricken, unforgiving. Messiaen’s Quartet for the End of Time, born in a prison camp, reaches beyond suffering toward eternity, where time dissolves into silence and praise. These works are fragments of memory, breath, and belief; resonating through the stillness that time leaves behind.

Program:
Dmitri Shostakovich – Piano Trio No. 2 in E Minor
Bela Kovacs – Sholem-Alekhem, rov Feidman!
Olivier Messiaen – Quartet for the End of Time

Photo by Marco Borggreve
